constitutions.title: My rules
constitutions.subtitle: Rules your agent must follow (budget, privacy, when to ask you).
constitutions.createSubtitle: Pick an agent and describe what it may or may not do.
constitutions.emptyBody: Without rules, almost everything is allowed. Add a simple limit first — you can refine later.
constitutions.formRequired: Choose an agent and a name for this rule set.
constitutions.noRules: No rules on the active version
constitutions.nextNegotiation: Next: start a negotiation to see the rules in action.
constitutions.activateHint: Draft constitutions must be activated before negotiations.
constitutions.noRulesHint: Create a new constitution with rule templates, or open Help.
constitutions.createFlowHint: Three things only: a name for this rule set, which of your agents it applies to, and at least one rule. Prefer the templates — they match what the policy engine really checks (amount, private data).
constitutions.rulesBuilderHint: Add one or more templates below. Change the number (threshold) if you want. Advanced fields are optional.
constitutions.ruleFieldsRequired: Each rule needs a field and a value.
constitutions.previewApproval: If a proposal goes over {x}, Legatio will pause and ask for your OK.
constitutions.previewDeny: If a proposal goes over {x}, it is blocked automatically.
constitutions.previewDefault: Add a template to see a plain-language summary here.
constitutions.savedActivated: Saved and activated. You can negotiate now.
constitutions.replaceBody: This agent already has an active constitution. Only one can be active at a time. Replace it with this one? The previous constitution will be archived.
constitutions.activateReplaced: Activated. The previous constitution was archived.
constitutions.rulesExplainerTitle: How a rule works (in plain words)
constitutions.rulesExplainer1: Each rule is: IF something is true in a proposal → THEN block it, or ask for your OK.
constitutions.rulesExplainer2: Start with templates. Example: “if the price is over 200, ask me first”.
constitutions.rulesExplainer3: DENY always wins over allow. If anything is unclear, the system prefers to stop or ask you — not to auto-approve.
constitutions.hintApproval: Good default: the agent may negotiate, but above this amount it must wait for you.
constitutions.hintDenyAmount: Hard ceiling: above this amount the proposal is refused — no negotiation around it.
constitutions.hintDenyPrivacy: Blocks the proposal if it asks for this one data field. Need more fields protected? Use “Block another data type”.
constitutions.hintCustom: Custom rules use technical field names the policy engine understands (e.g. amount, data_fields_requested). Prefer templates when unsure.
constitutions.advancedHint: Only needed for custom rules. Templates already set these correctly.
constitutions.agentHint: Rules apply to one of your agents. External/demo agents are listed elsewhere and are not selected here.
constitutions.noUserAgents: You still need to create your own agent before adding rules. External agents from the demo cannot carry your constitution.
constitutions.rulesPriorityNote: If one rule blocks and another would only ask for your OK, the block wins. That keeps risky actions from continuing.
constitutions.privacyValueHint: Must match exactly what the other party requests. Use a suggestion chip, or type the same technical token. One token per rule.
constitutions.privacyMultiHint: Each privacy rule blocks one data type only (that is how the engine works). To block phone and passport, add two rules — one per type. Same for any extra field.

negotiations.title: Negotiations
negotiations.subtitle: Talks between your agent and another party. Each round is checked against your rules.
negotiations.createSubtitle: Choose your agent, a counterpart, and the rules that protect you.
negotiations.emptyBody: Start one after you have an agent and rules. Demo installs often include a simulated company as counterpart.
negotiations.formRequired: Title, your agent, the other party, and a rule set are required.
negotiations.started: Negotiation started. You can process the first round.
negotiations.nextStart: Press Start to open the room, then process rounds one by one.
negotiations.nextRound: Process the next round to receive a new proposal and a policy result.
negotiations.nextApproval: A rule needs your decision. Open “Needs your OK” before more rounds can continue.
negotiations.detailSubtitle: Follow rounds below. Your rules decide allow, block, or ask you.
negotiations.needUserAgent: Create your own agent first (not only external demo agents).
negotiations.needExternalAgent: No counterpart found. Run demo seed data or add an external agent.
negotiations.proposalsHint: Each row is one offer checked by your rules. Private data requests appear in their own column.
negotiations.noProposalsBody: Press Start, then Process round. After each round you will see the amount and whether rules blocked, allowed, or asked for your OK.
negotiations.createExplainer1: Your agent talks to the other party in rounds (up to the max you set).
negotiations.createExplainer2: Every proposal is checked against your rules before anything continues.
negotiations.createExplainer3: If rules block, it stops. If they need you, it pauses for your OK. Nothing sensitive auto-approves.
negotiations.titleHint: A short name so you recognize this talk later.
negotiations.instructionPlaceholder: e.g. Stay under my budget and do not share my phone number
negotiations.instructionHint: Optional goal in your words. Hard limits still come from your rules, not from this text alone.
negotiations.userAgentHint: Only agents you created. External demo agents are not listed here.
negotiations.externalAgentHint: Usually a simulated company from demo data. This is who makes offers.
negotiations.rulesetHint: Must be the rules linked to your agent. This is what can block or ask for your OK.
negotiations.maxRoundsHint: Safety cap on how many back-and-forth rounds are allowed (default 10).

approvals.title: Needs your OK
approvals.subtitle: When a rule says the agent must ask you, it appears here. Nothing continues until you decide.
approvals.emptyBody: When a negotiation hits a limit (for example a high price), it will pause here for your yes or no.
approvals.decideHint: Approve only if you accept this proposal under your rules.

profile.title: Profile
profile.subtitle: Account settings, password and two-factor authentication
profile.saveFailed: Could not save profile (is PATCH /auth/me/ available?)
profile.passwordHint: Requires backend endpoint POST /auth/change-password/ (included in backend_profile_patch).
profile.twoFactorHint: Protect your account with an authenticator app (TOTP).
profile.scanQr: Scan this QR code, then enter a code to confirm.
profile.disable2faHint: Enter a current TOTP code to disable 2FA.
profile.avatarHint: Avatar is generated for demos (no upload yet).

agreements.title: Signed deals
agreements.subtitle: Final outcomes that were accepted and signed. You can verify integrity later.
agreements.emptyBody: After a negotiation ends with approval, a signed record can appear here.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.subtitle: A history of important actions. Useful if you need to check what happened.
audit.emptyBody: Events appear as you use negotiations and approvals.

agents.title: My agents
agents.subtitle: People or programs that negotiate for you. Start by creating one.
agents.createSubtitle: Give it a clear name — you can change details later.
agents.createHint: Tip: use a name you will recognize, e.g. “Travel helper” or “Subscription agent”.
agents.externalHint: Provided by the environment (seed). Use them as the other party in a negotiation.
agents.emptyMine: You don’t have an agent yet
agents.emptyMineBody: Create one first. Then you will add rules and start a negotiation.
agents.emptyExternal: No external agents visible. Run the seed script.
agents.nextConstitution: Next: add rules so this agent knows your limits.
agents.nameHint: Short name shown in lists and negotiations.
agents.descriptionHint: Optional. What this agent is for.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: How Legatio keeps you in control

steps.title: Create your agent
steps.body: From Dashboard or Agents — this is who negotiates for you.

steps.title: Define rules
steps.body: New constitution → templates → save and activate.

steps.title: Negotiate
steps.body: Start a room, process rounds, watch proposals and outcomes.

steps.title: Decide when asked
steps.body: Approvals badge in the menu means Legatio needs you.

faqs.a: Usually the constitution had no matching rules (or no rules at all). Add an approval threshold and activate.

faqs.q: Do I need JSON or code?
faqs.a: No. Use the constitution form templates and only edit the number.

faqs.q: What if I never open Approvals?
faqs.a: Actions that require your OK stay blocked. That is intentional.
In this MVP counterparties are simulated so you can test the full control loop safely.

help.rulesIntro: Rules look at proposal fields (like amount). Matching DENY blocks. Matching REQUIRE_APPROVAL waits for you. Otherwise ALLOW.
help.rulesHowToBody: Dashboard checklist → create agent → new constitution → use templates → save and activate → negotiate → process rounds → open Approvals if asked.
help.rulesExampleBody: Template “Ask my OK if amount > X” with value 200. Simulated offers of 600–800 will pause for you.
help.rulesActions: Prefer human OK for grey zones; hard DENY for absolute limits (privacy, extreme amounts).
help.rulesTip: Never leave a constitution with zero rules if you care about control — empty means almost everything is allowed.
help.promiseBody: Legatio is not the agent that books hotels or renews subscriptions by itself. It is the trust layer: you define rules, agents propose, policy decides allow / deny / ask you, and everything is audited.

glossary.meaning: A party in a negotiation. Yours is “your agent”; counterparties may be simulated in the MVP.
The rule pack attached to your agent. Must be Active to negotiate.
An offer in a round (amount, type, etc.) evaluated by policy.
A pause for your explicit yes/no when a rule requires it.
Signed outcome and immutable history of what happened.

help.intro: Legatio keeps you in control when an AI agent negotiates. You define rules; the system blocks or pauses unsafe actions; you approve when needed.

home.headline: Humans stay in control when agents negotiate
home.lead: Legatio lets you define rules, run multi-round negotiations, require human approval when risk is high, and keep a verifiable audit trail.

pillars.title: Constitutions
pillars.body: Policy rules your agents must obey: budgets, privacy, auto-renewal limits.

pillars.title: Negotiations
pillars.body: Structured rounds between your agent and external parties with clear outcomes.

pillars.title: Human-in-the-loop
pillars.body: High-risk proposals pause for approval. Agreements and audit close the loop.

home.bottomBody: Start with seed data or create your own agent in seconds. English and Spanish UI, light and dark themes.
